key_insight: In the infinite-width limit, regularized Newton and Gauss–Newton training drives PINN PDE residuals to zero despite the limiting kernel having no spectral gap.
engineering_relevance: The theory supports second-order optimization for neural PDE solvers and explains how regularization can mitigate gradient descent’s spectral bias.
method: Analyze regularized Newton and Gauss–Newton training as network width grows.
Derive deterministic limiting dynamics governed by a PDE-associated Newton neural tangent kernel.
Prove residual convergence and exponential decay on any fixed leading eigenspace for sufficiently small regularization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees with explicit width-limit rates, but no numerical benchmarks or datasets.
watch_item: The guarantees concern the overparameterized limit; finite-width implementations must also solve growing linear systems and, for Newton, handle potentially indefinite Hessians.
paper_title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
